what: Gallons of wall and ceiling paint, primer and tape for a room
title: Paint Calculator: How Much Paint Do I Need for a Room? | ProjectMath
description: Work out how many gallons of paint you need for walls and ceiling, minus doors and windows. Free paint calculator with primer, tape and a printable shopping list.
lede: Enter your room size to see how many gallons of paint to buy, after taking out doors and windows. The example room is 14 by 12 feet; change it to yours.

faq.q: How much paint do I need for a 12x12 room?
faq.a: A 12 by 12 foot room with 8 foot walls has 384 sq ft of wall. Take off one door and one window (about 36 sq ft) and two coats need roughly 2 gallons at 350 sq ft per gallon. Add a gallon if you are also painting the ceiling.

faq.q: How many square feet does a gallon of paint cover?
faq.a: Most interior paint labels say 250 to 400 sq ft per gallon for one coat. Smooth, primed walls get close to the top of that range; textured, porous or unpainted drywall uses more. This calculator uses 350 by default, and you can change it.

faq.q: Do I really need two coats?
faq.a: Usually yes. One coat often looks patchy, especially with a color change. Two coats give even color and the durability the manufacturer rates the paint for.
If you need more than about 4 gallons of one color, a 5-gallon bucket is normally cheaper per gallon and keeps the color consistent across walls.
Prime new drywall, patched areas, stained walls, glossy surfaces, and big jumps from dark to light colors. Clean walls already painted a similar color often need no primer.
